text.en: In a town by the seaside, Mini watched her Appooppan make a pot. He took clay, wetted it, pounded it and kneaded it like dough. Then he shaped it on a spinning stone wheel.

Mini watched her grandfather, Appooppan, make a pot.
He took clay and made it wet. He added enough water to get the right consistency. He pounded it well, so it was neither too watery nor too dry.
He kneaded the clay like dough and put it on a stone wheel. He shaped the pot by spinning the wheel.
When the pots were dry, Ammu moved them into a very hot oven called a kiln, where the fire baked them.
The family also made patterns on some pots to make them beautiful.
Visit a potter if you can and watch how the potter works.

problem.en: Order the steps of making a pot.

text.en: Knead and shape on the wheel.
Dry, then bake in a kiln.

prompt.en: Why is a pot baked in a kiln?
